source_links.title: 3D Bioprinting of Living Tissues
source_links.summary: Overview of vascularized engineered tissues, including SWIFT and co-SWIFT channel printing.
limitations: Broader bioprinting research; do not label SWIFT/co-SWIFT as SLA.
Does not establish a clinically transplantable whole organ.

source_links.title: TAU scientists print first ever 3D heart using patient’s own cells
source_links.summary: Reports a small vascularized heart construct made using patient-derived cells and biological materials.
limitations: Coordinated pumping had not been achieved at the reported stage.
Research construct; does not establish a transplant-ready human heart.

source_links.title: 3D Bioprinting: Growing a Child’s Own Ear in the Lab
source_links.publisher: Dr. Arturo Bonilla / Microtia – Congenital Ear Institute
source_links.summary: Participating investigator describes patient-cell-derived ear cartilage and an early human trial.
limitations: The page says the trial has concluded, but also retains an Active Clinical Trial badge; verify current status against a trial registry before reuse.
Trial authorization or device designation does not establish routine treatment approval or long-term efficacy.

source_links.title: 3D Bioprinting in Microgravity: Opportunities, Challenges, and Possible Applications in Space
source_links.summary: Perspective on opportunities and technical constraints of bioprinting in space, including light-based approaches.
limitations: Perspective article; does not demonstrate completed orbital SLA printing of living tissues.
Published in 2023; later developments require separate evidence.

source_links.title: 3D printing in microgravity paves way for biological bandages for astronauts
source_links.publisher: Berlin Institute of Health at Charité
source_links.summary: Reports light-cured skin-cell dressings tested during two parabolic-flight experiments with Cellbricks.
limitations: Parabolic-flight microgravity evidence, rather than an ISS experiment.
Does not establish clinical deployment of wound dressings for astronauts.

source_links.title: Development of 3D bioprinting: From printing methods to biomedical applications
source_links.publisher: Elsevier / Asian Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences
